items.title: Telangana govt removes unauthorised Ram statue from Basheerbagh, BJP dubs it ‘anti-Hindu’
items.summary: A statue of Lord Ram installed at Basheerbagh crossroads in Hyderabad for Dasara celebrations was removed by the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation, on October 24, Saturday, amid heavy police deployment. The statue was unauthorisedly installed by the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) along with demands to rename the crossroads as Sriram Chowk, triggering a controversy. The statue of the Hindu deity had been installed near the Kanaka Durga temple as part of its Navaratri festivities. However, following the objections raised by Majlis Bachao Tehreek (MBT) spokesperson Amjed Ullah Khan, the temple authorities removed the statue and loaded it onto a truck as directed by the civic authorities. The dispute began after VHP national spokesperson Ravinuthala Shashidhar, who is also general secretary of the Bhagyanagar Ganesh Utsav Samithi, called for the junction to be renamed. In a post on X on October 19, he wrote: “No longer Bashir Bagh, from today it is Sriram Chowk (sic),” and urged people to use the proposed name in their addresses.
